saying: Commenters accept directiveness as a continuum and say it should be judged by what an output functionally does—specificity, personalization, urgency, imperative force, omitted alternatives, confidence presentation—not by interface labels or disclaimers. Many ask that it be measured across multi-turn conversational trajectories, and several want anchored rubrics, worked examples, or decision trees for predictability.

disagreement.text: Most commenters want directiveness operationalized through new anchored levels, rubrics, or authority tiers; one argues against any new taxonomy, saying contested new terms would confuse manufacturers and directiveness should instead modify the existing benefit-risk factor of probability of harm.

sides.summary: Create explicit graded scales—anchored rubric levels, five-level authority tiers, or decision trees—with worked examples.
Avoid a new taxonomy; treat directiveness as a modifier within the existing benefit-risk probability-of-harm factor.
